text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, who stays as the head of caretaker government after President Liamine Zeroual accepted his resignation on Tuesday, is likely to be renamed prime minister in a coalition government.
- Security forces shoot dead four suspected bombers in Algiers.
- Morocco and Polisario representatives meet in London on talks over a U.N.-sponsored peace plan in the Western Sahara.
- Prime Minister Ouyahia resigns, sparking bargaining on his succession.
- Algerian court outlaws seven political parties for failing to adjust their policies to a party law.

- Prime Minister Ouyahia resigns, to stage his return in the government. President Zeroual has three options: renaming ongoing prime minister, appointing a new figure to breathe new dynamic into the government, or picking a politician enjoying wide support in the parliament.
- A new prime minister will be named after consensus in the parliament.
- Boualem Benhamouda, leader of the former ruling National Liberation Front, favours a coalition government in which all political parties will be represented.
